findings.title: Recommended project-hygiene files absent
findings.details: CONTRIBUTING.md, .editorconfig, and a dedicated docs/api/README.md are not present. Solo/pre-team projects can defer these, but they become blocking once a second contributor joins.
findings.action: Defer is acceptable at current team size (1); revisit before onboarding a second contributor. docs/appendices/A-api-spec.md already covers the docs/api/README.md role.

findings.title: PRD (Layer 1) has no dedicated Stakeholders/Personas section
findings.details: docs/PRD-SDD-v1.0.md §1.2 lists actors/use-cases but does not separately define stakeholders or end-user personas beyond the Zuri product persona (which is a system persona, defined in AGENTS.md, not a user persona).
findings.action: Add a short §1.2a Stakeholders section naming the actual human roles (e.g. SmartGift operator, Zuri platform owner) if/when more than one human role interacts with the system.

findings.title: SDD (Layer 2) has no Observability section
findings.details: The system has heartbeat, lease, and lifecycle-state concepts but no documented logging/metrics/alerting approach beyond stderr diagnostics.
findings.action: Add SDD §2.x Observability before S6 (worker) implementation — heartbeat/lease health is exactly the kind of thing that needs a monitoring story once the bridge runs unattended.

findings.title: SDD (Layer 2) has no dedicated Tech Stack or Error Handling Strategy section
findings.details: Tech stack (Node 22+, TypeScript, DuckDB, Zod) is stated only in the PRD executive summary; error-handling conventions are split across NFR-004 and Appendix A.4 without a consolidated statement.
findings.action: Low priority — content exists, just not consolidated. Fold into §2.1 or a new §2.1a on next revision.

findings.title: 12 of 24 tracked requirement IDs are marked not-yet-implemented
findings.details: FR-003/004/005/006/008, NFR-003/004/005, SEC-005, BR-005/006, and all 8 acceptance criteria (AC-001..008) are documented but have no implementing code yet (S5–S8 of the build order are pending).
findings.action: Not a doc defect — already tracked explicitly in docs/appendices/D-traceability.md §D.1–D.6 as planned/pending work against the S1–S8 build order. Listed here so it surfaces in a preflight pass too, not only buried in the appendix.

findings.title: 0 structured or unstructured requirement-ID references in source
findings.details: No file under src/ or tests/ carries an @req/@spec/@designs/@tested annotation or a plain FR-xxx/NFR-xxx comment. All D-traceability.md mappings are inferred from file purpose, not verified in-code.
findings.action: Already proposed in docs/appendices/D-traceability.md §D.7 with a worked example. Optional, not blocking — apply opportunistically as files are touched.

findings.title: Pre-existing docs use a different frontmatter convention than the new Document Control Block
findings.details: AGENTS.md, docs/COMMAND-AGENT-SPEC.md, and docs/AGENT-RUNTIME-SPEC.md use YAML frontmatter (id/version/status/owner/created_at/last_update) instead of the Document Control Block table + Version History used by the newly scaffolded docs. Both are internally consistent; they just don't match each other.
findings.action: Left as-is by design (doc-architect does not overwrite existing docs). Optionally standardize on one convention in a future pass — not urgent, no information is missing, only the format differs.

findings.title: Author identity differs between old and new docs
findings.details: Existing docs list author "ATHER"; newly generated docs list "Boss" (auto-detected from git config user.name). These may be the same person under a different handle.
findings.action: Confirm whether "ATHER" and "Boss" are the same author; if so, consider aligning the byline convention project-wide.

findings.title: A few frequently-used terms are not separate glossary entries
findings.details: "LINE Messaging API / LINE OA" and "idempotency key" are used repeatedly across docs but only appear inline inside other entries (e.g. under Flex), not as their own Appendix F rows. Appendix F is also not linked from the main docs/PRD-SDD-v1.0.md document.
findings.action: Add two glossary rows and one link from PRD-SDD-v1.0.md's document-authority section to Appendix F for discoverability.

findings.title: New catalog v4 spec/plan do not use the repository document-control convention
findings.details: The new SmartGift catalog v4 spec has status/date/owner prose and the implementation plan has no version-history block. They are review artifacts, but their control metadata is not yet aligned with the repository's established document conventions.
findings.action: Standardize version/status/owner/last-updated metadata before promoting the proposal to an approved implementation baseline.

findings.title: Catalog v4 acceptance IDs are not yet in the main traceability graph
findings.details: AC-A through AC-E and the catalog-specific ADR labels are scoped inside the new proposal documents; docs/.doc-graph.json and docs/appendices/D-traceability.md do not yet contain their nodes or implementation edges.
findings.action: Update the document graph and traceability matrix when the proposal is approved and implementation branches are merged; do not mark these criteria implemented from this docs-only PR.

findings.title: New catalog v4 documents have no relative Markdown links to validate
findings.details: The new spec and plan use code/path references and section references rather than Markdown links. External worktree paths are intentional and cannot be resolved inside this repository.
findings.action: Keep external worktree references synchronized as implementation moves; add repository-relative links when the referenced artifacts land here.

findings.title: Catalog v4 IDs are namespaced by acceptance group
findings.details: The new AC-A1 through AC-E3 labels do not collide with the existing FR/NFR/BR/SEC/DR/AC numeric identifiers; they remain proposal-local until traceability is updated.
findings.action: Preserve the namespace mapping when adding these criteria to the governed traceability graph.
